meta.title_plain: How a bedtime story for his son became Percy Jackson
meta.teaser: Rick Riordan's bedtime stories for his son turned into Percy Jackson and millions of books.

page.title: How a bedtime story for his son became Percy Jackson
page.bigIdea: Rick Riordan made up stories to help his son enjoy reading. One of them grew into a hero that millions of kids love.

cards.title: A kid who loved myths
cards.front: Rick was born in 1964 in San Antonio, Texas.
cards.back: The first book he read for fun was The Lord of the Rings, maybe ten times. He loved Greek and Norse myths from middle school.
cards.tryit: Pick one Greek god, like Zeus or Poseidon. Find one cool fact about them.

cards.title: First story at 13
cards.front: Rick started writing in middle school.
cards.back: At 13, he sent his first story to be published. It was turned down. He kept writing anyway and got his first stories printed in college.
cards.tryit: Write a short story opening in 5 sentences. Don't worry if it's messy.

cards.title: Teacher by day, writer by night
cards.front: For 15 years, Rick taught English and history.
cards.back: Mythology was his favourite lesson to teach. While teaching full time, he also wrote mystery novels for adults, and they won big awards.
cards.tryit: Explain one thing you know well to someone in under 2 minutes, like a teacher.

cards.title: Bedtime stories become Percy
cards.front: His son Haley asked for bedtime stories about Greek heroes.
cards.back: Haley found reading hard because of dyslexia. So Rick made his hero, Percy, dyslexic too, and turned the stories into The Lightning Thief in 2005.
cards.tryit: Tell someone a 2-minute story where your hero's 'weakness' turns into a superpower.

cards.title: From camp to Disney+
cards.front: A summer camp job gave Rick the idea for Camp Half-Blood.
cards.back: Today, over 190 million of his books are in print. He helped make the Percy Jackson show on Disney+ and won two Emmy Awards.
cards.tryit: Watch a Percy Jackson trailer. Spot one Greek myth idea in it.

words.d: Old stories about gods and heroes, told by ancient peoples like the Greeks.
In myths, a child of a god and a human.
A different way the brain handles words, which can make reading harder.
A set of books that tell one big story, in order.
A top prize for the best TV shows and the people who make them.

opts: As bedtime stories for Rick's son
quiz.hint: Look at card 4. Think about the time of day.
quiz.why: Rick made up stories about Greek heroes at bedtime for his son Haley.

quiz.q: Why did Rick make Percy dyslexic?
opts: His son Haley had dyslexia too
quiz.hint: Who was the very first listener of the story?
quiz.why: He wanted his son to see a hero who was a bit like him.

quiz.q: What happened to the first story Rick sent out at 13?
quiz.hint: Card 2 is about not giving up.
quiz.why: It wasn't published, but he kept writing and later became a bestselling author.

quiz.q: Where did the idea for Camp Half-Blood come from?
opts: His job at a summer camp
quiz.hint: Think about what Rick did during college summers.
quiz.why: He worked as a music director at a summer camp for three years in college.

page.think: Percy's dyslexia turns out to be part of his strength. What's something that feels hard for you that could also be a hidden strength?
